cases.sentence: На запотевшем стекле чьим-то пальцем было написано: «…» – и вот в эти просветы я увидел ___, много огней и уплывающую станционную надпись «Покров».
cases.explain: «городские огни» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: I looked out the window. Now the old blackness beyond the window was no longer there. On the sweaty glass someone’s finger had marked: ". . . ."’ And through these little gaps I caught sight of city lights, lots of city lights and a station sign swimming past—"Pokrov."’

cases.explain: «Петушинского района» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "Pokrov! A town in the Petushki Region. Three stops and then Petushki. You’re on the right path, Venedikt Erofeev." And then my alarm, which had risen from the bottom of my soul, started back toward the bottom of my soul and fell quiet there. But then something else started up again from the bottom of my soul—one thought, one monstrous thought rushed upon me so that I felt weak in the knees.

cases.explain: «верном пути» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: "Pokrov! A town in the Petushki Region. Three stops and then Petushki. You’re on the right path, Venedikt Erofeev." And then my alarm, which had risen from the bottom of my soul, started back toward the bottom of my soul and fell quiet there. But then something else started up again from the bottom of my soul—one thought, one monstrous thought rushed upon me so that I felt weak in the knees.

cases.explain: «яркие огни» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Here I am leaving the Pokrov Station. I saw the sign "Pokrov’"’ and the bright lights. All this bodes well, both "Pokrov" and the bright lights. But why did they appear on the right side of the train? I admit that my reason is in a bit of an eclipse, but, really, I’m no kid, I do know that if the Pokrov Station appears on the right it means I’m going away from Petushki toward Moscow and not away from Moscow toward Petushki. Oh, that mangy sphinx! I was struck dumb and started to rush about the car; as luck would have it there wasn’t a soul init. ‘"‘Hold it, Venichka, don’t rush it. Stupid heart, don’t beat. Maybe you've gotten a little confused, maybe Pokrov was on the left and not the right after all? Go on out and take a better look at what side of the train the glass was marked on."’

cases.sentence: И – сразу – рассеялась тьма, в которую я был погружен, и забрезжил рассвет из ___ души и рассудка, и засверкали зарницы, по зарнице с каждым глотком и на каждый глоток по зарнице.
cases.explain: «самых глубин» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: And so I threw back my head and drank up my last drop. And right away the dark into which I had been plunged cleared away, and dawn broke in the very depths of my soul and my reason, and sheet lightning glimmered once for every swallow.

cases.sentence: В первом – не было никого, только брызгал дождь в ___.
cases.explain: «открытые окна» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: And I set off through the train. No one was in the first car; rain splashed in through the open windows. In the second there wasn’t anybody either; the rain wasn’t even splashing in.
